newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia calls Australian "sore loser" over Games.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia calls Australian "sore loser" over Games.

text.p: Malaysian sports officials denied on Saturday that Kuala Lumpur used "the power of money" to win its bid to host the 1998 Commonwealth Games, as alleged by an Australian sports official.

Siah Kok Chi, honorary secretary of the Olympic Council of Malaysia, said Australian Commonwealth Games Secretary-General Arthur Tunstall sounded like a "sore loser" for making claims he could not back with evidence.
"I can assure you there was no hanky panky, there was no money. There was no secret fund hanging around," Siah told Reuters.
"If he (Tunstall) has any evidence, he should have brought it up. He sounds to me like a sore loser and nothing else," Siah said in a telephone interview.
Kuala Lumpur in 1992 beat Adelaide for the right to host the Games and is spending more than $500 million to build facilities and run the 10-day sporting festival.
Malaysia sees the Games -- the largest event it has ever hosted -- as important to its international image.
Australian media on Saturday reported Tunstall as saying Malaysia had won the bid through "the power of money".
"It was unfortunate the power of money and other influences won the day," the Sydney Morning Herald quoted him as saying.
"I've got a fair idea what went on but I'm not prepared to talk about how much money or anything else was given but yes, it was more than a T-shirt," Tunstall said.

Australia and Malaysia have had stormy relations in the past. Relations hit a low in 1993 after then Australian Prime Minister Paul Keating calling Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad "recalcitrant" for skipping the inaugural Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Seattle.
Siah said Malaysia had spent five million ringgit ($2 million) on its bid, including bringing international sports officials to Kuala Lumpur to show off its facilities.
